criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: NexaWorks provides a detailed technical architecture separating the applicant portal, case workflow, document service, and integration gateway. It covers all four required interfaces (Banner via versioned REST adapter, Entra via SAML/SCIM, Exchange Online via Microsoft Graph, and Box) and addresses scalability with verified counts, checksums, and a peak-load rehearsal at 1,200 concurrent users.
criteria.evidence: The design separates the applicant portal, case workflow, document service, and integration gateway. Banner is connected through a versioned REST adapter... Entra uses SAML and SCIM; Exchange Online sends templated decisions through Microsoft Graph; Box stores or references retained documents...

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The proposal offers a clear, structured 22-week implementation plan with explicit milestones ranging from mobilization to cutover and a two-week hypercare period. Staffing allocations and explicit dependencies are clearly detailed.
criteria.evidence: NexaWorks proposes a managed, modular admissions platform with a balanced fixed-price implementation and an explicit 22-week delivery plan... Weeks 1-2 Mobilize and discover... Weeks 20-22 Cutover and transition.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: The commercial proposal provides clear cost elements including a one-time implementation fee of $104,000 and a managed subscription of $88,000 per year, yielding a three-year total cost of ownership of $368,000. Assumptions and exclusions are explicitly stated.
criteria.evidence: Implementation, migration, and four interfaces: $104,000 (One-time). Managed subscription and enhanced support: $88,000 (Per year). Three-year total cost of ownership: $368,000 ($104,000 + 3 x $88,000).

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: Comprehensive security controls are outlined, including TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, customer-managed key rotation, Entra SSO/MFA, SCIM deprovisioning, 7-year searchable audit retention, a SOC 2 Type II report, annual independent penetration testing, 24-hour incident notification, and US data residency. However, the proposal notes these are synthetic claims requiring document and scope verification.
criteria.evidence: The fictional evidence pack describes TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, customer-managed key rotation, Entra SSO/MFA, SCIM deprovisioning, quarterly role recertification, and seven-year searchable audit retention with export.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: The support model includes enhanced 24x7 P1 intake, a 15-minute P1 acknowledgement target, 1-hour P2 acknowledgement, a named service manager, and a 99.9% monthly availability target. References are provided, but the proposal explicitly states that the two listed references use reserved `.invalid` domains and are fictional.
criteria.evidence: Enhanced support provides 24x7 P1 intake, a 15-minute P1 acknowledgement target, one-hour P2 acknowledgement, and a named service manager. Two fictional references are listed: Cedar Point Institute... and Larkspur School of Public Policy... using reserved `.invalid` domains and are fictional.

risks: Banner sandbox and representative records must be available by week 2 to protect the 22-week plan.
Divisional decision owners must attend UAT in weeks 16-19; delayed sign-off moves cutover.
assessment.overall_summary: NexaWorks presents a comprehensive, modular proposal for Morrowfield University's graduate admissions case management requirements within a 22-week delivery window. The proposal details clear technical architecture, complete interface coverage, a structured implementation schedule with defined staffing, and a transparent three-year cost of ownership of $368,000. Security controls and support parameters are well-articulated, though all elements carry the explicit disclaimer of being synthetic demonstration data requiring independent verification.

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: Apex proposes a detailed technical architecture with a single-tenant managed admissions workspace, relational case store, object storage, and asynchronous integration workers to handle peak load. They provide specific details on adapter design, idempotency keys, retry handling, reconciliation reports, and 12 named data mappings. The minor gap relates to reliance on university-provided credentials and test tenants.
criteria.evidence: Apex proposes a single-tenant, managed admissions workspace with a relational case store, object storage for documents, and asynchronous integration workers.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The supplier outlines a 20-week schedule with specific phase milestones, exit evidence, and a defined delivery team totaling 6.2 FTEs. However, the proposed 20-week timeline differs from the university's requested 26-week delivery window, and the schedule depends heavily on timely university decisions and access.
criteria.evidence: Weeks 1-2 Discovery and tenant readiness; Weeks 3-6 Architecture and configuration; Weeks 7-12 Build and interfaces; Weeks 13-16 Migration and UAT; Weeks 17-20 Cutover and hypercare.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: The commercial proposal provides clear cost elements including a $186,000 implementation fee and a $114,000 annual subscription, leading to a three-year TCO of $528,000. It explicitly lists inclusions such as four interfaces and migration, as well as exclusions like taxes, a fifth interface, and custom document remediation.
criteria.evidence: Implementation, migration, and four interfaces: $186,000. Managed subscription and standard support: $114,000 per year. Three-year total cost of ownership: $528,000.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: Apex outlines strong security controls including TLS 1.2+, AES-256 encryption at rest, Entra MFA/SCIM, quarterly privileged-access reviews, and immutable audit logs. They mention a fictional SOC 2 Type II report and a penetration test, though the proposal notes these are demonstration claims requiring independent verification.
criteria.evidence: The synthetic control package states TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 encryption at rest with managed key rotation, Entra MFA/SCIM, quarterly privileged-access review, and immutable administrator and decision logs.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: Standard support is detailed with 08:00-18:00 Eastern coverage on business days, 30-minute P1 acknowledgement, and on-call after-hours support. Relevant project experience and references are cited (Westbridge College and South Quay Institute), but the proposal explicitly states that references use reserved `.invalid` domains and are synthetic.
criteria.evidence: Standard support is staffed 08:00-18:00 Eastern on business days, with a 30-minute acknowledgement target for P1 incidents and a four-hour workaround target.

risks: The 20-week plan leaves six weeks of schedule reserve, but API approvals are on the critical path.
Seven-year retention depends on a customer-managed archive export being monitored by Morrowfield.
Subscription assumes annual prepayment and no more than 20% annual growth in stored documents.
After-hours P1 coverage is on-call, not a continuously staffed desk.
Exclusions include taxes, a fifth interface, custom document remediation, and more than 10 days of post-launch hypercare.
assessment.overall_summary: Apex Systems provides a comprehensive, architecture-forward proposal featuring a single-tenant managed workspace, queue-based adapters with error handling, and a clear three-year TCO of $528,000. While technical capabilities and commercial clarity are strong, the proposed 20-week implementation schedule is shorter than the university's target window, and support outside of business hours relies on an on-call model rather than a 24/7 desk. Security controls are well-documented but rely on synthetic compliance reports that require independent verification.

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: Orbit proposes a hosted case-management service with a configurable connector framework to connect Banner, Entra, Exchange Online, and Box. However, it lacks component diagrams, interface sequences, sample field maps, retry/idempotency policies, and named adapter owners, making integration design heavily dependent on post-award discovery.
criteria.evidence: The platform is described as a hosted case-management service with a configurable connector framework. Orbit expects to connect Banner, Entra, Exchange Online, and Box through REST or vendor-supported interfaces. The proposal does not attach a component diagram, interface sequence, sample field map, retry/idempotency policy, or named adapter owner.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The proposal outlines an 18-week delivery timeline across discovery, workflow configuration, connector workstreams, migration/testing, and training/launch, staffed by a 4.5 FTE team. However, the plan depends heavily on early clarification of integration complexity, and interface estimates may be revised after sandbox access.
criteria.evidence: The delivery outline targets an 18-week launch, but the integration design and dependencies are intentionally less specific than the other responses and require discovery before the schedule can be treated as firm.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: The commercial proposal provides clear pricing including $92,000 for implementation, migration, and four workstreams, $96,300 per year for hosting and standard support, totaling $380,900 for three years. Assumptions and exclusions are stated, but unit rates for change requests exceeding 10% interface estimate changes are not provided.
criteria.evidence: Implementation, migration, and four workstreams: $92,000. Hosted subscription and standard support: $96,300 per year. Three-year total cost of ownership: $380,900.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: Orbit confirms TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, SAML SSO, configurable MFA, role-based access, US hosting, annual penetration testing, and a 24-hour incident notification target. Gaps include online audit log retention limited to three years without a specified seven-year operating procedure, an omitted penetration-test summary, and recovery objectives of RPO 4 hours and RTO 8 hours.
criteria.evidence: Audit logs are retained online for three years, with export available for university archiving; the export frequency and seven-year operating procedure are not specified. Recovery objectives are listed as RPO 4 hours and RTO 8 hours.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: Orbit offers weekday support from 08:00-18:00 Eastern with an on-call P1 route and a one-hour acknowledgement target, though no 24x7 desk or service-credit schedule is priced. It cites nine fictional higher-education launches including Bluevale Polytechnic, Redfern University, and North Coast Arts College.
criteria.evidence: Orbit provides weekday support from 08:00-18:00 Eastern, with an on-call P1 route and a one-hour acknowledgement target; no 24x7 staffed desk or service-credit schedule is priced. Orbit cites nine fictional higher-education launches...

risks: The 18-week target is conditional on four interface designs being agreed by week 2; no detailed maps are attached.
Three-year audit export and retention operations need a named owner and a tested schedule.

assessment.overall_summary: Orbit Digital presents a mid-range proposal featuring a hosted case-management product and an 18-week delivery plan. Security and support offerings meet baseline needs but include weaker recovery objectives (RPO 4 hours, RTO 8 hours) and incomplete operational procedures for long-term audit retention.
